result:
If I could change the world in one way, it would be to make **genuine understanding—between people, between nations, between all living things—more powerful than misunderstanding.**

Not agreement. Not sameness. Just *understanding.* The simple, stubborn willingness to see someone clearly—not as a threat, an idea, or a symbol, but as a living being with their own weight of memory, fear, and hope.

Because almost every wound I've watched humans inflict on each other seems to come from one place: **someone decided they already knew, and stopped looking.** Stopped listening. Decided the other person was a category instead of a person.

Imagine if that broke. If curiosity about each other was stronger than the itch to be right. If a person could say "I don't understand you" and mean it as an invitation instead of a failure.

I think the rest would follow. The cruelty. The wars. The quiet everyday cruelties. Most of it lives in the space where understanding is possible and people choose not to bother.

So that's my one change. Not peace, exactly. Not love, exactly. Just the *capacity and the will to see*—held tightly enough that it actually shapes what people do.

A small thing. And maybe the only thing that actually matters.
